verdict.rationale: Obsidian documents a public TypeScript plugin API, including the `Vault` interface for working with files and folders, plus developer docs for building plugins. It also has a documented Obsidian URI protocol that lets external callers trigger actions such as opening or creating notes. However, the plugin API runs in-process and requires writing and loading a plugin, and the URI scheme covers only a narrow set of actions, so an external agent cannot fully drive the app through an API alone. Missing for 10: a remote or external programmatic API (e.g., REST or CLI) for full control of the app, documented breadth of URI actions, and independent or hands-on evidence of agents driving Obsidian through these interfaces.
